info.title: memory-ledger
info.description:
The local HTTP API over one person's memory graph.

**It calls no model.** Every endpoint here is the graph engine behind a socket:
plain SQL through `graph.py`'s `api_*` helpers, so everything it does is
token-free. Leaving a client polling it costs nothing.

## Security — read this before changing `--host`

**The write API is unauthenticated.** There is no token, no session, no CSRF
protection. Anything that can reach the port can rewrite the graph.

- The default bind is `127.0.0.1`. Keep it there.
- If you must expose it (`--host 0.0.0.0` for phone access), pass `--no-write`:
  every `POST` then returns 403 and `/api/meta` reports `writable: false`, which
  is what makes the UI hide its editing controls.
- Do not put it behind a plain reverse proxy and call it done; that publishes an
  unauthenticated write API to whoever can reach the proxy.

## Conventions

- Every response is JSON with an `ok` boolean; failures carry `error`, and the
  error is the reason worth showing a person rather than a status code.
- String inputs are length-capped server-side. Over-long values are truncated,
  not rejected.
- Open vocabulary (`realms`, `kinds`, node `types`) is read from `/api/meta`,
  never shipped in a client. Closed sets (`rels`, `statuses`) are enforced here.
- A disconnected client is not an error: the map polls, so a reload aborts a
  response mid-write, and the server returns silently rather than reporting a
  500 down a socket that has already closed.

Node.description: One node of the graph, as the map draws it.

type.description: OPEN vocabulary — the engine never restricts it.

realm.description: Empty is normalised to the server's default realm.

kind.description: props.kind, or the none-token for a node carrying none.

degree.description: How many edges touch it — the map sizes the dot by this.

rel.description: A CLOSED set, enforced on write. See /api/meta.

NeighbourEdge.description: An edge seen from one node, so it carries its direction.

TaskRow.description: The slim row the date views return — small on purpose.

due_local.description: The due date resolved into the brain's timezone, or '--' when there is none.

RealmCount.description: Two counts, because they answer different questions: `nodes` is what the map filters over, `open_tasks` is what the dashboard filters over.

SectionShape.description: One heading of a contract shape (CONVENTIONS §5.1, §5b.1). The UI builds its forms from these rather than hard-coding the headings — a heading written into the page would be a second definition of the shape, and the one nothing checks.

generated.description: Rendered from the declarations; the form leaves it out.

Skill.description: A skill contract, with its children nested by `requires` and nothing else (CONVENTIONS §5a).

why.description: Three different questions. `declared` is what the skill says it is accountable for; `matched` is what match-rules hands it at runtime; `always` is a non-negotiable, appended to every match.

scenario.description: The cue match-rules actually fires on — not the body.

cue.description: The wording in the text that produced this guess.

exists.description: This brain already holds it — the only interesting case.
